Harness homes, declared links, settings, and session-state hygiene

## Setup

Run `just setup` once per checkout, and once on each host after pulling a change to the
recipe; it is idempotent. The repository git config it writes (`filter.harness-state.*`
included) lives in the synced checkout and is shared between hosts.
It installs the git hooks and the harness-state filter (`filter.harness-state.clean`,
`required = true` so a failing clean stops git instead of staging live picks, and the
identity `smudge = cat`, without which git fails every checkout of a required-filter
file), and creates `local/codex/rules/`. Work settings under `local/` come from another
configured host; setup creates directories, not private settings.

## Gates

Run `just test` before committing: tt records the complete four-partition suite under
the local host worker budget. Policy remains absent/enabled during hosted preparation.
Use `just test-one <pytest arguments>` for focused tests; tt preserves arguments and
runner status through the budget. `just test-full` explicitly forces the broad route.
The relay signal test stays serial; xdist reads the grant's worker count. `just ci-test`
shares the suite but requires explicit positive PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS and never
sets TT_FORCE. The prepared workflow sets it at job scope, uses two workers and retains
setup and suite artifacts. Hosted coverage has not been accepted; the
three proposed integration omissions are listed in docs/test-execution.md.
Both pre-push routes run
mandatory `just check-hygiene` followed by `just test`; no outer composite is timed.
The hook declares origin branches covered for the prepared workflow and warns on
uncovered pushes when local policy skips tests; the declaration is not remote evidence.
`just ci-hygiene` runs the portable subset without registry-dependent ops-check.
See [test execution](docs/test-execution.md) for report retention and coverage checks.
The pre-commit hook refuses staged paths under
`local/`, then runs `tools/ops-check` over the working tree (the hygiene checks ops
projects share: guide references, conflicted copies, agent scratch, machine layout and
adopted copies), then checks the guide identity regions with `tools/ops-docs check`, and
last exports the staged tree once for the staged `tools/harness-facts check` and the
staged `.githooks/harness_state.py check --staged-tree`. The latter validates
`harnesses.toml` and `.gitattributes` as staged, refuses a staged harness config blob that
still holds what the filter strips (fix with `git add --renormalize <path>`), and refuses
when the repository's filter config is not what `just setup` writes (`clean`,
`required = true`, `smudge = cat`; read from the shared config in a linked worktree too). A record commit
that the hygiene checks refuse means a finding somewhere in the working tree, not in the
record. A new attachment that carries host values follows the attachment fallback in
lore `skills/references/retained-item-records.md`: keep the raw bytes under WORK_ROOT
and attach a portable derivative. Never widen `.ops-check.toml` for an attachment.
`just docs` regenerates the identity regions from `identity.toml`.

The hook's explicit `--ci` mode retains staged-local-state refusal, docs validation
and both staged checks over one export, omitting only ops-check. Full local checks
remain mandatory in the default hook, `check-hygiene` and both pre-push routes.

From main, `just link` previews home changes and `just link-check` checks convergence.
`just mods` validates and tests the Claude Code mods when the Claude CLI is available.
The generated global Projects block is checked by lore.

## Layout

- `links.toml` and `tools/harness-links`: real harness homes, declared home links and
  their reconciliation through the tasks project registry.
- `claude/`, `codex/`, `agy/` and `local/`: harness settings, hooks, skills registries and
  untracked host state. `agy/hooks.json` routes lifecycle and `before-tool` events through
  `relay`, while `agy/hook` heals detached `agy` settings files and adapts `SessionStart`
  (profile, capture-notice) and `Stop` (claim-guard until ops-33cef9 lands). `claude/mods/` holds
  Claude Code function-hook plugins; `claude/probes/` the probes behind Claude Code facts.
- `harnesses.toml`: the declared harnesses (`[harnesses.<name>]`) and, for each tracked
  live config, its `[harnesses.<name>.live_state]`: path, filter glob, the keys and tables
  the clean filter strips, and the pick units `live-picks` saves. `.gitattributes` routes
  exactly those globs to the filter.
- `.githooks/`: config-state filtering, Codex trust and model pick preservation, and commit
  checks, all reading `harnesses.toml` through `.githooks/harness_state.py`, whose `check`
  validates the manifest, `.gitattributes` and the filter config.
- `facts/capabilities.toml` and `tools/harness-facts`: what each harness has been shown
  to do, with the record behind each value. The tool is the only reader; it takes the
  declared harness names from `[harnesses]` in `harnesses.toml`.
- `agents/skills/session-logs/`: session-store guidance. `agents/bin/` keeps
  session-episodes, wake-judge and their tests.
- `pi/`: the pinned pi install (`just pi-install`), its launcher, the `settings.json`
  its home links to, the pick-preserving `pi/extensions/harness-state.ts`, and the probes
  behind the `pi` and `pi-durable` facts. A version change reruns the probes (README.md).
- `relay/`: the pinned relay runtime (`just relay-install`) and its launcher.
- `tools/session-archive` and `systemd/user/`: transcript capture and pruning.
- `tools/hq` (`tools/hq_cli/`, flags in `tools/hq.toml`): `hq sessions` lists and resumes
  sessions across harness homes from their own metadata (README.md).
- `docs/`: specs, plans, notes, runbooks, a commit map in rewrites/, and frozen documents
  moved to lore and flows, kept for closed tasks. `tools/ops-docs` and `tools/ops-check`
  are vendored from ops.

The global instructions, profiles and general skill corpus live in lore. This root
file is hq's project guide; home links to global instructions target lore.

## Rules

- Change home routing in `links.toml`. Apply with `just link --apply` from main only;
  linking to a worktree would leave live harnesses dependent on temporary storage.
  Targets must exist in their registered owner checkouts before an apply.
- Keep `local/` untracked. It contains work settings, rules and saved Codex trust;
  publishing it would expose host and work state.
- Treat model picks, effort and Codex trust as live state. The clean filter and trust
  hooks preserve their contract; avoid stashing or overwriting main's harness configs
  merely to clear a modified marker. See README.md for the recovery behavior. While
  `harnesses.toml` is broken, git commands that run the filter fail closed: restore the
  manifest (`git checkout -- harnesses.toml`), never unset `filter.harness-state.required`.
- Enable session-archive timers only on a host with its archive configuration and
  backup destination. Archive tests must use temporary stores rather than live logs.
- Read a capability fact through `tools/harness-facts` (`get`, `list`, or its `lookup`
  as a module), never by parsing the file. Edit the file in a worktree; `unknown` is an
  answer and never a default. README.md has the re-probing procedure.
